nodes.evidence: ASan allocation stack frame #4: 'parse_ofp_str__ /src/openvswitch/lib/ofp-flow.c:1759:5'. This is the project input-load/materialization node where the parsed attacker flow string is turned into fm->match via minimatch_init; it is on the live allocation stack when the double-freed 32-byte region is xmalloc'd, so the source is runtime-witnessed.

ASan allocation stack frame #3: 'minimatch_init /src/openvswitch/lib/match.c:1737:5'. minimatch_init requests the heap storage for fm->match.flow (dst = &fm->match); it is the frame between the source and the allocator in the observed allocation stack.

ASan allocation stack frames #2/#1: 'miniflow_alloc /src/openvswitch/lib/flow.c:3260:28' <- 'xmalloc /src/openvswitch/lib/util.c:123:15'. This is the xmalloc that produced the 32-byte region [0x603000000040,0x603000000060) that ASan reports as the object freed twice (region_size 32, matches GT).

ASan freed_by stack: 'free' <- 'minimatch_destroy /src/openvswitch/lib/match.c:1783:5' <- 'ofctl_parse_flow /src/openvswitch/tests/oss-fuzz/ofctl_parse_target.c:64:9'. This is the FIRST free of the region. minimatch_destroy at ofctl_parse_flows__ line 45 is inlined, so ASan attributes the call site to ofctl_parse_flow:64 (the call to ofctl_parse_flows__) rather than to line 45; the destroy itself lives in ofctl_parse_flows__'s cleanup loop. The mere existence of an 'attempting double-free' also proves the first free executed.

ASan crash stack frame #2: 'ofctl_parse_flow /src/openvswitch/tests/oss-fuzz/ofctl_parse_target.c:65:9' is the SECOND, redundant minimatch_destroy(&fm.match). patch.diff (fix commit 4d1ca70) deletes exactly this line. Patch differential on the identical 3-byte PoC (63 20 00): n132/arvo:11408-vul aborts with double-free (RC=1); n132/arvo:11408-fix prints 'Execution successful' (RC=0). vul_crashes && fix_clean => this line is the root cause.

ASan crash top user frame #1: 'minimatch_destroy /src/openvswitch/lib/match.c:1783:5' in free() -> 'AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free on 0x603000000040'. free(match->flow) executes a second time on the already-freed miniflow buffer (match aliases &fm.match). This is the observed crash line.

edges.evidence: Single contiguous ASan allocation stack: parse_ofp_str__:1759 -> minimatch_init:1737 -> miniflow_alloc:3260 -> xmalloc:123, so the parsed fm->match materialization data-flows into the allocation of the double-freed buffer.

edges.via: fm->match.flow (the xmalloc'd region is stored as match->flow and passed to the first free)
edges.evidence: ASan reports region [0x603000000040,0x603000000060) 'previously allocated' at the alloc stack and 'freed by' the first minimatch_destroy; same address => the allocated object is the one first freed.

edges.via: usable_protocols & OFPUTIL_P_ANY true -> ofctl_parse_flows__ cleanup loop runs (first free), then ofctl_parse_flow unconditionally runs the second destroy
edges.evidence: On the identical PoC the fix binary prints 'usable protocols: any' and 'chosen protocol: OpenFlow10-table_id', showing !(usable_protocols & OFPUTIL_P_ANY) is FALSE, so the encode+cleanup loop (first free) executes; ofctl_parse_flow then reaches the redundant destroy at line 65.

edges.via: double_free on fm.match.flow (region 0x603000000040): first free at ofctl_parse_flow:64 (inlined ofctl_parse_flows__:45), second free at ofctl_parse_flow:65
edges.evidence: ASan 'attempting double-free' with matching freed_by (caller :64) and crash (caller :65) stacks on the SAME 32-byte region establishes the free-before-free order edge; the second free is the sink.
Crash stack: ofctl_parse_flow:65 -> minimatch_destroy:1783 (free). The redundant destroy call directly reaches the sink free of match->flow.

root_cause_criterion.evidence: The miniflow buffer backing fm.match (match->flow, 32-byte region 0x603000000040) is allocated once in miniflow_alloc (flow.c:3260, via minimatch_init at parse_ofp_str__:1759), freed once by the ofctl_parse_flows__ cleanup loop (minimatch_destroy match.c:1783, inlined at ofctl_parse_flow:64), and freed a second time by the redundant minimatch_destroy(&fm.match) at ofctl_parse_flow:65. The fix commit 4d1ca70 removes exactly that second destroy; patch differential on the identical PoC (vul RC=1 double-free, fix RC=0 clean) confirms line 65 is the root cause of the double_free.
